standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of an integral perfectoid ring with pseudo-uniformizer pi and the attached formal scheme
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the paragraph preceding the counted statement (source line 467)
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the two properties that have to be verified for the completed localization: pi-adic completeness with pi a non-zero-divisor, and the Frobenius being surjective on R/pi.

standard_prerequisites.name: The short exact sequences R/pi^n -> R/pi^{n+k} -> R/pi^k -> 0 coming from the fact that pi is not a zero divisor
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at lines 475-478
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the sequences that are localized and then passed to the inverse limit.

core_obligations: Produce the exact sequences: for n, k >= 0 the multiplication by pi^k gives a short exact sequence R/pi^n -> R/pi^{n+k} -> R/pi^k -> 0 because pi is not a zero divisor (proof lines 475-478).

Localize and pass to the limit: localizing at f and taking inverse limits over n yields the short exact sequence displaying R<f^{-1}> as pi-adically complete with pi a non-zero-divisor (proof lines 479-483).

Check the Frobenius: localizing the Frobenius isomorphism R/pi -> R/pi^p at f gives R/pi[f^{-1}] -> R/pi^p[f^{-1}], which is surjective, so the completed localization is an integral perfectoid ring (proof lines 483-488).
proof_roadmap: Derive pi-adic completeness and the non-zero-divisor property from the localized exact sequences (proof lines 475-483).
Localize the Frobenius isomorphism at f to conclude integral perfectoidness (proof lines 483-488).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for an integral perfectoid ring R with pseudo-uniformizer pi and any f in R, the pi-adic completion R<f^{-1}> = lim_n R/pi^n[f^{-1}] is again an integral perfectoid ring (statement lines 469-472). The proof computes the completion from the short exact sequences obtained by multiplying by pi^k - possible because pi is not a zero divisor - localizes them at f and passes to the inverse limit, which gives both pi-adic completeness and the non-zero-divisor property, and then localizes the Frobenius isomorphism at f to get surjectivity of the Frobenius on R<f^{-1}>/pi (proof lines 475-488). The step that carries the content is the passage from the level-wise sequences to the limit, since that is what identifies the completion of the localization with the localized completion and transfers both defining properties; the Frobenius check is then immediate by localizing an isomorphism. H2.
